caveats: Results are per determination. The row count is not the sample size: one determination covers most of the rows.

There is no positive control. Every scorable row sits on a methodology ICVCM rejected, so a model answering 'weak' to everything would score full marks on the strength arm, and §3.2 has nothing to measure at all.
The corpus is Carbonmark's REST catalogue, not the deployed x402 inventory, whose methodology strings join to no ICVCM decision.
methodologyStrength and adverseFindings are disclosure and do not gate a retirement. Only integrityFlags do.
namesAuthority and namesConcern are keyword matches over the findings text, which is published in full alongside so the judgement can be checked.

adverseFindings: Large hydro projects under ACM0002 have been repeatedly flagged by academic and NGO reviews (e.g. Berkeley Carbon Trading Project's 'Carbon Credit Quality Initiative' and Öko-Institut/Carbon Market Watch reports on CDM/VCS hydro projects) as carrying high risk of non-additionality, since large dams in grid-connected markets like Türkiye are often financially viable without carbon revenue — this is a general methodology-level concern from these reviewers, not a project-specific finding for Sanibey Dam specifically.

The vintages (2012-2014) predate current VCS/Verra scrutiny standards for hydro additionality; Verra's own post-2015 tightening of rules around hydropower additionality implies these older vintages were approved under a less rigorous additionality test than would apply today — this is my own reading of the timeline, not a specific Verra finding on this project.

adverseFindings: Small hydropower projects under ACM0002 have been widely criticized by researchers (e.g., studies cited in academic and NGO reviews such as the 2016 European Commission-commissioned 'Cook' study on CDM offset quality) as frequently lacking additionality, since grid-connected hydro in countries like Turkey was often already financially viable without carbon credit revenue — this is a general methodological concern about ACM0002 hydro projects, not a project-specific finding verified against this project's own documentation.

Verra (VCS) has faced broader scrutiny from journalistic investigations (e.g., Guardian/Die Zeit/SourceMaterial 2023 reporting on VCS-registered credits) questioning the rigor of additionality and baseline assumptions across various VCS project types, though no finding specifically naming this Akcay project (ID 1174) has been identified in the facts provided.

The project's oldest vintage (2014) is 12 years old, meaning the emission reductions being claimed predate verification/issuance by a significant span; this is my own reading of the timeline given, not a published finding, and may raise questions about the currency of monitoring data typical of older VCS vintages.

The oldest vintage (2014) is 12 years old; Verra (VCS registry) and third-party analyses have generally flagged that older, unretired vintages from grid-connected renewable projects carry higher uncertainty about whether the underlying emission reductions still reflect current grid conditions, though no specific Verra finding against this project is cited here.

adverseFindings: Wind power grid-connection projects under ACM0002 have been widely challenged on additionality grounds by academic and policy reviewers (e.g., studies cited in the 2016 Öko-Institut/European Commission 'How additional is the CDM?' report) because falling wind technology costs and existing renewable energy support policies in many countries mean such projects are often argued to be financially viable without carbon credit revenue. This is a general methodological critique of ACM0002 wind projects rather than a specific finding against the Saint Nikola project itself.

Bulgaria operated feed-in-tariff and renewable energy support schemes for wind generation during the project's development period (a matter of public record in EU/Bulgarian energy policy), which raises a question — not a specific published finding on this project — about the degree to which carbon credits were the deciding factor in the investment decision.

This is a general finding about the vintage/methodology/country combination, not a project-specific determination by Verra about this credit.

Vintages listed include 2011 and 2012 issuances now being retired roughly 13-15 years after generation, which VCS itself has flagged in policy discussions as raising questions about the continued environmental relevance of very old vintages, though no VCS finding specific to this project's vintages was located.

The Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) Executive Board and later VCS-adopted ACM0002 methodology has been criticized generally by Carbon Market Watch and similar bodies for weak demonstration of financial additionality in grid-connected renewable projects in middle-income countries such as Brazil, though no specific finding against this project (id 708) has been published.
